title: Cross-region sticky-session healing plan and customer comms for escalated Dedicated tenants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported persistent 503/timeout behavior after a partial cross-region network degradation. Root cause appears to be ‘sticky session’ state pinned to unhealthy regional proxies combined with KV-cache divergence for routing tokens. This ticket defines a safe, staged healing and tenant rehome procedure, a short-term hotfix for session pinning, and a customer communication plan. Goal: restore affected tenants to normal traffic paths without mass disruption, ensure observability and rollback hooks, and document follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: Simulate partial region egress degradation (packet loss ~10-20% to region eu-west-1) while leaving control-plane healthy
Issue traffic to multi-tenant endpoints with sticky-routing enabled (tenant routing header + session cookie) at typical peak QPS
Observe amplified tail latency and 5xx rates for tenants with connections pinned to the degraded region
Trigger KV-cache rollback to older routing snapshot to force re-evaluation of active node set and observe routing mismatches
mitigation_steps: 1) Immediate: Enable per-tenant temporary override to bypass sticky-session for new connections (feature-flag toggle: ff.routing.temp_bypass_sticky)
2) Controlled drain: Mark unhealthy regional proxies as draining for matched tenant slices using staggered 30s windows to avoid cache stampedes
3) Telemetry gating: Turn on higher-fidelity traces for affected tenant IDs and enable request sampling @100% for 10 minutes
4) Failback: After stabilization, re-enable sticky routing via rollout gate and monitor for reappearance of 5xx or latency regressions
runbook_steps: A. Detection: Alerts fire from dashboards (5xx_rate > 2% over 5m for tenant) and sticky-session imbalance metric > 1.5x
B. Triage: SRE lead confirms region degradation using netperf and control-plane health checks; declare customer-impacting incident if >1 high-paying tenant affected
C. Stage 0 (non-invasive): Flip ff.routing.temp_bypass_sticky for affected tenant(s) via Console feature flags - target traffic reroutes to healthy pool within 60s
D. Stage 1 (drain): For tenants still impacted, drain sessions from unhealthy proxies by adjusting proxy weight: set weight 0 -> monitor 2m -> set administrative drain = true

E. Stage 2 (rehoming): If drain fails, initiate tenant rehome to warm standby region using tenant-pin reassign API with gradual connection handoff (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 10 minutes), validate KV cache integrity at each step
F. Rollback: If errors spike, rollback rehome in reverse with 5-minute observation windows; escalate to oncall managers if rollback fails
G. Post-incident: Collect KV snapshots, sticky-session mappings, and per-tenant traces for root-cause analysis
communication_plan: Customer comms: Draft initial notification template for affected Dedicated accounts — include impact, mitigation in progress, expected window, and point-of-contact (SE/CSM)
Internal comms: Incident channel #incidents-cross-region and pager duty escalation to SRE oncall + PMs for Dedicated customers
Status updates cadence: 15m for first hour, 30m afterwards until resolved; public status page update if more than 1 hour
Post-incident: 1:1 customer debriefs for high-revenue tenants and a postmortem summary to accounts and support teams
hotfix_notes: Hotfix A (short-term): Accept new connections without reading legacy sticky cookie; apply at edge to force new routing decisions. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7892
Hotfix B (safety): Add circuit to limit rehome rate per tenant to 5 connections/sec to avoid DB/KV overload. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/3410
Rollout plan: Canary 1% in staging -> 10% prod -> 50% -> 100% with 10-minute health windows
postmortem_actions: 1) Implement a sticky-session health score that decays automatically when region-level packet-loss is detected
2) Add automated KV cache cross-checker that validates routing snapshots between regions every 5 minutes
3) Improve Console runbook UI to allow per-tenant one-click staged rehome with preflight checks
4) Create a synthetic canary that exercises sticky routing across regions on a rolling basis
5) Update SLA runbooks and enterprise KB for Dedicated customers with clear escalation matrix
acceptance_criteria: Runbook validated in a tabletop exercise with SRE, Platform, and Customer Success
Feature-flagged sticky-session bypass implemented and tested end-to-end
Automated alerts and dashboards for sticky imbalance added to prod observability
Customer communication templates approved by Legal and GTM
